## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Easing
//
// Easing functions shape the rate of change of an animated value: pure maps from
// normalized time in [0, 1] to normalized progress. Progress is nominally in
// [0, 1], but the Back and Elastic families intentionally overshoot. Keyframes,
// tweens, and transitions select easings by ClassicEasing or carry one of the
// parameterized easing records declared here.

// The family (base shape) of a non-linear classic easing curve.
type EasingFamily
    = Quad | Cubic | Quart | Quint | Sine | Expo | Circ | Back | Elastic | Bounce;

// The phase of a classic easing curve: where its acceleration is
// concentrated. In accelerates from rest, Out decelerates to rest, InOut
// accelerates then decelerates.
type EasingPhase = In | Out | InOut;

// Selects a curve from the full classic easing catalog: either the identity
// (Linear) or one of ten families in one of three phases (QuadIn, BounceOut,
// ElasticInOut, ...).
type ClassicEasing
    = Linear
    | Eased(Family: EasingFamily, Phase: EasingPhase);

// A CSS-style cubic Bezier easing. The curve's endpoints are pinned at (0, 0)
// and (1, 1); P1 and P2 are the two free control points. P1.X and P2.X lie in
// [0, 1] so the curve remains a function of time; Y components may leave [0, 1]
// to overshoot. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve)
type CubicBezierEasing
    implements IValue, IEasingFunction
{
    P1: Number2;
    P2: Number2;
}

// Where the jump occurs within each interval of a stepped easing, following
// the CSS steps() model: rise at interval start, at interval end, neither
// endpoint (Steps must exceed 1), or both endpoints.
type StepPosition = JumpStart | JumpEnd | JumpNone | JumpBoth;

// A staircase easing that advances in a fixed number of equal jumps rather than
// continuously. Steps is at least 1.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step_function)
type StepEasing
    implements IValue, IEasingFunction
{
    Steps: Integer;
    Position: StepPosition;
}

// A polynomial smoothstep easing with zero derivatives at both endpoints.
// Order selects the polynomial: 0=linear, 1=cubic smoothstep (3t^2 - 2t^3),
// 2=quintic smootherstep; order N yields a polynomial of degree 2N + 1 with N
// vanishing derivatives at each end. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoothstep)
type SmoothstepEasing
    implements IValue, IEasingFunction
{
    Order: Integer;
}

// Parameters of a damped spring used for physical-feeling motion. All three are
// unitless tuning values for animation feel, not physical quantities. The
// spring is critically damped (no oscillation, fastest settle) when Damping
// equals twice the square root of Stiffness times Mass.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damping)
type SpringParameters
    implements IValue
{
    Stiffness: Number;
    Damping: Number;
    Mass: Number;
}

// Shape parameters for the Elastic easing family. Amplitude scales the
// overshoot (1 or greater; 1 is the classic curve); Period is the oscillation
// period as a fraction of the total duration (classic value 0.3).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator)
type ElasticParameters
    implements IValue
{
    Amplitude: Number;
    Period: Number;
}

// Shape parameter for the Back easing family. Overshoot controls how far the
// curve pulls back before advancing (or overshoots past 1); the classic value
// is 1.70158, which overshoots by about 10 percent.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overshoot_(signal))
type BackParameters
    implements IValue
{
    Overshoot: Number;
}

// Shape parameters for the Bounce easing family. Bounces counts the rebounds
// after the initial fall; Restitution is the fraction of height retained by
// each successive bounce.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_restitution)
type BounceParameters
    implements IValue
{
    Bounces: Integer;
    Restitution: Proportion;
}
```
